subject: Conditional headroom for Zephyr pilot — tiered burst request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Zephyr Health <zephyr-ops@zephyrhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional headroom for Zephyr pilot — tiered burst request

Team — looping you all in on a short, conditional request from Zephyr Health (pilot / live demo next week). TL;DR: they need a predictable temporary headroom allocation in a dedicated GPU slate for a 3-hour live demo where they expect a high-concurrency burst. We can either grant a soft-guarded headroom window or force them onto a strictly quantized fallback model.

Key details from Zephyr:
- Scheduled demo: Tue 2027-09-14, 10:00–13:00 PT
- Expected peak concurrent sessions: ~220 (sustained ~10m windows)
- Model: medium LLM (~13B) for canonical flows; fallback model available (7B quant)
- Must have <1200ms 95th pct latency for demo flows

What I'm proposing (product asks & constraints):
1) Temporary headroom slice of 8 GPUs from our dedicated pool for the window, triggered by request ID ZHP-4471.
2) Autoscaler exception: allow burst policy to raise concurrency cap for Zephyr project by 3x for the window, with automatic rollback after 3 hours.
3) Safety gates: (a) cost cap of $X for window (proc to confirm billing code), (b) fallback to 7B quantized model if 95th > 1.2s for more than 2 consecutive 15m checks.

Asks to the thread:
- Marcus: can you please validate feasibility and real expected tail-load on the runtime? Any risk to other customers?
- Dev: can the autoscaler be given a temporary exception and an automatic rollback hook? What ops steps are required?
- Laura / Hannah: is product comfortable with the canary gating and cost cap? If yes, I'll align Zephyr and procurement.

Attached: zephyr-pilot-runbook.pdf, headroom-metrics.yaml

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Zephyr Health <zephyr-ops@zephyrhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional headroom for Zephyr pilot — tiered burst request

Kimberly — thanks for the summary. Quick notes from runtime/infra perspective:

- The peak concurrency you listed (~220) for 13B will push sustained KV cache memory significantly and could impact co-tenants if we don’t isolate the slice. Allocating a strict 8-GPU dedicated slate (isolated) is the safe option.
- Autoscaler exception: doable, but we need two changes: (1) raise the per-tenant concurrency limit in the scale policy for the slate; (2) set an enforced rollback cron job to revert policy after the window. Both are low-risk but require a 24–48 hour ops change freeze window for safe rollout.
- Fallback model: highly recommended to pre-stage the 7B quant on the same slate and validate that token-per-second throughput meets demo SLO. Switching mid-window is non-trivial but acceptable if we automate the trigger.

Questions:
1) Is the 8-GPU number firm? If we can keep to 6 GPUs plus aggressive KV-sharing and prefetch we might reduce cost exposure. I attached a quick capacity-impact.csv with modeled tail latencies at different allocations.
2) Who owns the billing cap enforcement? Procurement needs a coding mechanism (chargeable project id) or we have to do manual tracking.

I'll standby to run a dry canary on Friday if we get approval.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional headroom for Zephyr pilot — tiered burst request

Kimberly / Marcus — I like the safety-first approach. A few product constraints and suggested changes:

- Gate by SLO: make the headroom activation conditional on the canary hitting baseline latency (<900ms p95) in the 30 minutes prior to demo. If canary fails, we push demo to quantized model with an agreed script for the Zephyr team to justify to their stakeholders.
- Canary: propose a 30-minute canary starting 09:15 PT on demo day (45 minutes before the official start). Marcus — can you run that?
- Cost cap: product can sign off on a $2,500 demo cap (subject to finance approval). Procurement needs to provide a billing tag.

Hannah — please prepare an ops-runbook snippet that includes rollback steps and a public-facing message template for Zephyr in case we need to cut to fallback. Danielle in CS will need that to manage expectations.

If we have signoff today I can confirm with Zephyr and escalate procurement.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Console

Subject: Re: Conditional headroom for Zephyr pilot — tiered burst request

All — ops side: we can implement the autoscaler exception and scheduled rollback with the following plan:

1) Create a temporary policy entry scoped to project ZHP-4471 with a raised concurrency cap and an explicit TTL that triggers policy-revert via our infra-controller.
2) Pre-stage the 7B quant on the same slate as Marcus requested; that takes ~90 minutes to warm (doable Friday dry-run).
3) Implement the canary job (09:15–09:45 PT) that runs synthetic flows and publishes p95 to the runbook channel. If p95 > 900ms, the canary job sets a flag and infra-controller will automatically redirect traffic to quantized model.
4) Billing: we require a charge code (procurement tag). Without it, finance will not approve charge.

Ops ETA: 24 hours for policy changes + 12 hours to pre-stage models + final dry canary on Friday (09/10). If product and procurement confirm the billing tag today, we can commit to the Friday dry-run and Tuesday demo.

Dev Patel
Platform Engineer, Serving Ops
Redwood Inference
